rubric_items.reason: Every S-n/ACm appears in a covers list. S-4/AC4 is only weakly tested: TP-16 checks that the section is hidden, not that the other sections and actions are unchanged. S-3/AC4's same-as-hand-picked check is not tested directly.

API rules are tested at integration level with Supertest. Page rendering and ?date= handling are unit tests with Testing Library. That is the cheapest level that proves each one, and no e2e tests are planned.

There are negative tests for PATCH ignore, invalid ?date=, entry keys and the 404, plus good boundaries (UTC vs local midnight, free 0, all passed). Missing: POST body ignore (EP-4) and the recomputed field in the availability PUT response (EP-5).

Tools match the strategy and the web test file is named. Test titles start with 'API:'/'Web:' instead of a requirement ID, which goes against the requirement-ID rule the plan cites. No API test file is named.
Titles are concrete and runnable, with exact clocks and dates. A few are ambiguous: TP-19 says 'not echoed', and TP-14 names 'validDay', a symbol absent from the design and module map.

findings.text: S-4/AC4 requires every section and action of an Inactive doctor's page to be unchanged, but its only test, TP-16, checks only that the Next 7 days section is absent. TP-17 covers the unchanged-sections regression for active doctors only (S-4/AC2).

cites.quote: then every section and action on the page is the same as on the build before this change
Web: no 'Next 7 days' section when nextSevenDays is null (Inactive doctor)

findings.suggested_fix: Add a unit test that renders an Inactive doctor with upcoming appointments and checks that the other sections and actions are still present and unchanged. Map it to S-4/AC4.

findings.text: The design makes the POST and availability PUT responses carry nextSevenDays, and says the field is ignored in a POST body. The plan has a negative test only for PATCH (TP-19). Nothing tests POST-body ignore or the recomputed field in the PUT response.

cites.quote: computed for the new doctor. The field is ignored in the request body.
computed from the new availability
API negative: nextSevenDays in a PATCH body is ignored and not echoed

findings.suggested_fix: Add integration tests showing that POST /api/doctors ignores nextSevenDays in the body, and that PUT /api/doctors/:id/availability returns nextSevenDays built from the new blocks.

findings.text: The plan says every test name starts with its HMS-9 requirement ID, but each title starts with 'API:'/'Web:' and no test is mapped to a REQ-n. Existing tests use names like 'HMS-7 REQ-8: ...'.

cites.quote: Every test name starts with its HMS-9 requirement ID (C3).
HMS-7 REQ-8: the read-only count in a PATCH body is ignored

findings.suggested_fix: Give each TP an 'HMS-9 REQ-n:' prefix derived from the story trace, for example 'HMS-9 REQ-2: ...' for TP-1.

findings.text: S-3/AC4 requires the 16 Nov day schedule opened via the link to match what it shows when 16 Nov is picked by hand. TP-12 checks only 14 Nov setting the date, and TP-11 checks only the link href.

cites.quote: shows exactly what it shows today when 16 Nov is picked by hand
Web: opening /doctors/:id?date=2026-11-14 sets the day schedule date to 2026-11-14

findings.suggested_fix: Add a check to TP-12 (or a new test) that opens ?date=2026-11-16 for a day without availability and compares the result with picking 16 Nov by hand.

findings.text: TP-20 (entry keys and the 404) and TP-19 (PATCH ignore) are mapped to S-1/AC2 and S-4/AC2. Those criteria are about counts matching the day schedule and other sections being unchanged, so the mapping overstates what these tests cover.

cites.quote: API negative: each entry holds only date, available, booked, free; unknown doctor is still 404

findings.suggested_fix: Trace TP-19 and TP-20 to the design endpoints (EP-1, EP-3) and to REQ-10, rather than to S-1/AC2.

findings.text: TP-19 says nextSevenDays is 'not echoed', but under the design the PATCH response does carry nextSevenDays, computed after the update. A tester could read the title as 'the response omits the field'.

cites.quote: nextSevenDays in a PATCH body is ignored and not echoed
The response carries `nextSevenDays` as in EP-1, computed after the update.

findings.suggested_fix: Reword the title: the sent value is ignored, and the response holds the computed nextSevenDays.

findings.text: TP-14 names a web helper 'validDay' that the design never names. The design only says the parameter must hold a valid YYYY-MM-DD.

cites.quote: is ignored; validDay rejects it
when it holds a valid `YYYY-MM-DD`, else from `todayIn(timeZone)` as now

findings.suggested_fix: Describe the behaviour without naming a symbol, or cite where validDay exists in the web package.
